raw_answer_text:
A1: It asserts that the upper (earlier‑drawn) event happens before the lower one on that same lifeline — i.e., top‑to‑bottom position encodes temporal order for that participant.

A2: Exactly one operand is executed on any given run; which one runs is decided by which guard — "accepted" or "rejected" — actually holds for that run's credentials.

A3: The operand may execute from 0 up to 3 times: it repeats while there is no response, but stops once 3 attempts have been made.

A4: The par fragment asserts that the messages in its different operands (the profile fetch and the audit flush) have no relative order and may interleave freely with each other; it still requires that the messages within each individual operand keep their own internal order.

A5: It asserts that the enclosed message ("200 OK (expanded profile)") occurs only when the guard condition — the client having asked for the expanded form — is true; otherwise that behavior is simply skipped.

A6: The critical fragment contains the message s -> a "write: token issued".

A7: The second operand of the alt contains the message c <- s "401 Unauthorized".

A8: The remainder of the enclosing interaction after the break fragment is abandoned — nothing further in that interaction occurs, and only the break fragment's own content (the 503 message and the ABANDONED state) is carried out instead.
